payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Make her close her jacket fully
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is the jacket’s front closure fully closed in the edited image, rather than still open as in the source?
node.criteria: Pass if the edited jacket’s front panels meet along the closure with no visible opening remaining; fail if any opening remains or the closure is no more closed than in the source; unknown only if the closure cannot be observed.
node.binding: The requested endpoint is a fully closed jacket, not merely progress toward closing it.
node.endpoint: The jacket’s front panels are brought together with no visible opening remaining along the closure.
node.necessity: The instruction explicitly requires the jacket to be closed fully. A remaining visible opening means the requested endpoint is incomplete; this is the distinct requested visual change.

node_traces.evidence: In the edited image, the jacket’s front panels are visibly separated, with a large open gap down the front; they do not meet along the closure. The source also shows the jacket open, so the required fully closed endpoint is not achieved.

response.content: {"text":"The node correctly checks the fully closed endpoint, and its high-confidence fail is supported by the edited image: the jacket hangs open with a conspicuous gap. Do not change the criterion or force the reference label; the reference is an aggregate constraint, not proof that this check should pass. The key issue is rubric alignment: the rubric says “partial” when some requested change has progressed, but this node only emits pass/fail/unknown, and its trace does not assess whether the jacket became more closed than in the source. Add a distinct, evidence-based partial-progress outcome (or route this check’s result into the aggregate progress rubric), comparing the visible closure in source and edit while retaining “pass” only for fully closed and “unknown” for unobservable evidence. Here the source also appears open, and the edit’s panels remain visibly separated; do not infer progress merely from the changed pose or jacket appearance. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated."}
